essays.title: Free search first, then pay by product count
essays.thesis: The spread in Shopify AI search bills is not about AI. It is about what each app counts.
essays.dek: Six search apps, three sample stores. A large store pays $0, $139, $376.25 or $436 a month depending on whether the app meters products, search requests or sessions.
sections: The question

A store owner on r/ecommerce asked something we hear a lot: native Shopify search misses typos, but every search app "scales up way too fast based on catalog size or clicks." So is the free app enough, and if not, which bill grows slowest?

From the official pricing pages, checked 26 Oct 2026 on monthly billing, a large store pays $0 for Shopify Search & Discovery, $139 for Searchanise, $376.25 for Algolia and $436 for Doofinder. Boost and Fast Simon stop publishing prices above the small store.
Start with the free one

Shopify Search & Discovery is $0 at every size. It gives you synonyms, product boosts and filters. Pull your zero result searches, clean up titles and tags, add synonyms, then decide. If you skip that step, a paid app just indexes the same messy catalog.
Four apps, four meters
Searchanise counts products. Unlimited searches. $19 small (500 products), $39 medium (5,000), $139 large (25,000).
Algolia counts search requests, and search as you type sends one per keystroke. $8.75 small, $87.50 medium, $376.25 large, before any developer time.
Doofinder counts search requests too, in plan steps. $186 for both small and medium on Pro, then $436 on Advanced.
Fast Simon counts all store sessions. Essential is $114.99 for the small store (up from $99.99 in October). Above 30,000 sessions there is no public price.
So a busy Black Friday does nothing to a Searchanise bill, and quite a lot to a per request bill. That is the "scales too fast" feeling, and it depends on your meter, not your catalog quality.
Where prices go dark

Boost starts at $29 for the small store. Its public pages put Convert at about $239 to $299 for our medium store, but the exact sub tier is not public, so we do not put a number on it. Fast Simon is the same above 30,000 sessions. Klevu and Nosto publish no volume price at all. If a vendor makes you ask, we mark it not public rather than guess.
The verdict

Small store: stay on free Search & Discovery until you have proof search is losing sales. If you need typo tolerance, Searchanise at $19 or Algolia at $8.75 are the cheapest paths, but Algolia needs someone technical.
Medium store: Searchanise at $39 is the lowest published price for a no code app. Algolia at $87.50 makes sense only if you have a developer.
Large store: Searchanise at $139 is still the lowest published bill. Algolia and Doofinder cost roughly three times that on our numbers, and they buy you more control, not a cheaper bill.
One caveat: our request count assumes about 1.5 search requests per session. Your theme and traffic can move that a lot, so check the pages below with your own numbers before you commit.

essays.title: AI support under $50 a month?
essays.thesis: Price the support app at the size you will be in a year, not the size you are today.
essays.dek: At 200 chats a month nothing paid with a real AI agent comes in under $50. At 1,000 chats most bills grow 3x to 5x, and the ranking reshuffles.
sections: The question

A store owner on Reddit asked for the cheapest AI chatbot that actually works for a small Shopify store, on a budget under $50 a month. Our small store gets 200 support conversations a month, has one person answering, and the AI handles half. Here is the cheapest plan that covers it, from official pricing pages checked 26 Oct 2026.
Under $50, only the free one fits
Shopify Inbox: $0. Free, with an AI sales associate trained on your catalog, policies and store content.
Helpcenter: $40. Cheap, but it gives you AI-written FAQs, not an AI agent.
Chatty: $59.99. Basic is $19.99 for 100 AI conversations. The other 100 cost $0.40 each.
Tidio: $68. Lyro costs $39 for up to 200 conversations, plus Tidio's $29 plan for the chats a person answers.
Zipchat: $80. Starter gives you 750 AI replies, which Zipchat says is about 300 conversations.

After that come the full helpdesks in a tight $109.75 to $138 band: Re:amaze, Freshdesk, HubSpot, Gorgias and Intercom Fin. Start with Shopify Inbox, and pay for an AI agent only when you need one inbox for email, social and returns.
What 5x the chats does to each bill

Move the same store to 1,000 conversations a month and two seats. Gorgias goes from $130 to $670 (5.2x), Re:amaze from $109.75 to $474.50 (4.3x), Zendesk from $259 to $1,118 (4.3x), HubSpot from $120 to $420 (3.5x) and Chatty from $59.99 to $199 (3.3x).

Two apps barely move. Richpanel goes from $319 to $478 (1.5x), because a small store already pays its $200 AI minimum, so it climbs from 10th to 5th among paid AI apps. Siena AI goes from $840 to $1,200 (1.4x), because most of its bill is the $750 platform fee.
The one that is cheapest now may not be cheapest then.
What counts as "one"

Chatty bills per AI conversation. Tidio counts a conversation once Lyro sends a reply, whether or not it solves anything. Zipchat counts every AI reply, and a back and forth uses about 2.5 of them. Re:amaze, HubSpot and Zendesk bill only when the AI resolves the conversation. Two stores with the same number of chats can get very different bills.
